text.p: Sonat Inc's exploration program is starting 1997 with a $400 million capital budget, Chief Executive Ronald L Kuehn Jr said Wednesday.
This compares to the $382 million spent in 1996, he told the PaineWebber Energy conference, noting Sonat started last year with an exploration budget of $325 million.
He said the 1997 budget calls for spending of $86 million on exploration and $285 million on development activities, adding, "I would be very surprised (if those numbers) don't increase."
Kuehn said exploration and production will account for more than half of Sonat's operating earnings in 1997, up from 44 percent in 1996.

He said the company is projecting a 15 percent increase in oil and natural gas production adding, "it wouldn't surprise me if we exceeded that." He noted that each $0.10 per 1000 cubic feet change in the price of natural gas is equal to $0.14 per share change in Sonat's annual earnings.
Kuehn said the company's Southern Natural Gas pipeline has $150 million of expansion projects on the boards.
This includes an extension to the Huntsville-Decatur, Alabama area which is expected to be completed this year at a cost of $56 million.
He said the pipeline's rate base is projected to grow to $990 million by the end of 1998 from $785 million at the end of 1996.
